items.definition:
(of language) used in ordinary or familiar conversation; not formal or literary
His speech was full of colloquial expressions.

relating to or characteristic of a particular religious denomination
The school is not denominational and welcomes students of all faiths.

always producing the same result
The algorithm is deterministic, meaning it will always produce the same output for the same input.

relating to a doctrine or belief
The church's doctrinal teachings are very strict.

asserting opinions as facts
His dogmatic approach to problem-solving left no room for discussion.

having a strong, exciting, or intoxicating effect
The heady scent of jasmine filled the air.

disturbing and horrifying because of involvement with or depiction of death and injury
The artist created a series of macabre paintings.

relating to the heart muscle
The patient suffered a myocardial infarction.

representing things as they are in nature; realistic
The artist's naturalistic style captured every detail.

done with great care and thoroughness
The restoration of the old painting was a painstaking process.

relating to the ability to interpret or become aware of something through the senses
The study examined perceptual differences between groups.

having many sexual partners; indiscriminate
The term "promiscuous" can be used to describe someone who has many casual sexual partners.

having only magnitude, not direction
Temperature is a scalar quantity, while velocity is a vector.

relating to the body, especially as distinct from the mind
Somatic cells are any cells in the body other than reproductive cells.

mutually beneficial
The relationship between the two companies was symbiotic.

equivalent in seriousness; virtually the same as
His silence was tantamount to an admission of guilt.

relating to thermodynamics
The engine's efficiency is governed by thermodynamic principles.

relating to veins
The blood sample was taken from a venous source.

relating to a ventricle (of the heart or brain)
The patient suffered from ventricular fibrillation.

extremely bad; appalling
The team's performance was abysmal, losing by a huge margin.

Relating to or denoting the fifth period of the Paleozoic era, during which coal deposits were formed.
The Carboniferous period is known for its vast coal swamps.

Hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed.
He gave the report only a cursory glance before signing it.

extremely unpleasant or difficult
The journey through the desert was hellish.

having both male and female characteristics or organs
The term 'intersex' refers to individuals born with reproductive or sexual anatomy that doesn't fit typical definitions of male or female.

having or showing a wish to do evil to others
The villain's malevolent gaze sent shivers down her spine.

burdensome; involving a great deal of effort, trouble, or difficulty
The task of cleaning the entire house was onerous.

spending money or resources freely and recklessly; wastefully extravagant
The prodigal son returned home after wasting his inheritance.

remarkably or impressively great in extent, size, or degree
She showed prodigious talent at a very young age.

advocating or implementing gradual reform rather than abolition or revolution
The party adopted a more reformist approach to economic policy.

taking effect from a date in the past
The pay raise was made retroactive to January 1st.

advocating or practicing revision of a previous theory, belief, or historical account
His revisionist interpretation of history sparked much debate.

never giving up; persistent
The heat was unrelenting, even at night.

relating to plants or growth
The patient was in a persistent vegetative state.

relating to the Andes mountains
The Andean condor is a large South American bird.

relating to or produced by color; (in music) relating to or using notes not belonging to the diatonic scale
The artist used a wide chromatic range in her painting.

relating to the forces or properties that stimulate growth, development, or change
The system exhibits complex dynamical behavior.

straying from the proper course or standards; behaving wrongly
The errant knight was on a quest to find adventure.

impossible to repair
The damage to the ancient manuscript was irreparable.

relating to milk or lactic acid
Lactic acid builds up in muscles during intense exercise.

relating to a larva
The larval stage of the insect is very different from the adult.

not biased or partisan
The committee aims to be completely nonpartisan.

harmful, poisonous, or very unpleasant
The factory emitted noxious fumes into the air.

rich and luxurious or lavish
They lived in an opulent mansion with many servants.

domineering; unpleasantly arrogant
Her overbearing attitude made it difficult to work with her.

having a sharply strong taste or smell
The pungent odor of garlic filled the kitchen.

full; well-supplied
The book is replete with fascinating details.

extremely distasteful; unacceptable
The idea of cruelty to animals is repugnant to me.

lacking courage or determination; weak
He was too spineless to stand up for himself.

loyal, reliable, and hardworking
He was a stalwart supporter of the team.

stretched or pulled tight; not slack
The rope was pulled taut.

lasting forever; immortal
He pledged his undying love to her.

leaving no doubt; unambiguous
The answer was an unequivocal 'no'.

impossible to understand or measure
The depths of the ocean are unfathomable.

not celebrated or praised
She was an unsung hero, working tirelessly behind the scenes.

relating to a ruler who has absolute power
The company was run by an autocratic leader who made all decisions.

Relating to the fourth period of the Paleozoic era, between the Silurian and Carboniferous periods.
The Devonian period is known as the "Age of Fishes."

Of or relating to an ellipse; oval.
The planet orbits the sun in an elliptic path.

former; previous
His erstwhile friend now ignored him.

(of a person) lean and haggard, especially because of suffering, hunger, or age
After the illness, he looked thin and gaunt.

produced by inbreeding; inherent
The small community suffered from inbred genetic issues.

relating to or characterized by the process of deriving general principles from particular facts or instances
Inductive reasoning moves from specific observations to general conclusions.

characterized by or given to introspection; examining one's own thoughts or feelings
He spent a lot of time in introspective thought, reflecting on his life.

Relating to the Messiah; characterized by fervent hope or belief in a messiah.
The leader had a messianic complex, believing he was destined to save the world.

Lower in position.
He descended into the nether regions of the cave.
